change.title: Open the claim page with a warm 'hope it made you smile' instead of a cold coupon header
change.targets: Claim page: landed → gave email (first-paint engagement)
change.expected_effect: A plausibly small lift in landed→gave email by keeping first-paint warmth continuous, most likely inside the noise floor at this traffic. Honestly framed as a compounding bet, not a provable win.
change.why_it_helps: The gift box that made someone scan is warm and playful, but the page used to answer with a cold 'You've Got 30% Off / Enter your email' — and our session recordings show most people leave without ever touching the form. Opening in the box's own warm voice keeps that good feeling alive for one more beat, so more people lean in and reach the email box instead of pattern-matching 'marketing form' and closing the tab.
changes_in_plain_words: The big headline on the claim page now says 'Hope it made you smile' instead of 'You've Got 30% Off' — it greets people the way the gift box did, before mentioning the reward.
The little line above the reward list changed from the flat 'Enter your email to receive' to the friendlier 'Add your email and we'll send'.

Nothing else moved: the 30%-off code, the free personalized video, the email box, and the 'Send Me My Code' button are all exactly where they were — the discount is still shown right below the new headline.

previews.label: the claim page — the screen people see right after scanning the QR code on the box

change.why_the_rate_is_what_it_is: The email ask is an EXCHANGE: the visitor gives an email (a small cost + mild distrust) to get the discount code + video. The rate is the price being accepted. Converters accept because the warmth/curiosity carried over from the box makes the reward feel worth a tap; non-converters, provably, mostly never even reach the point of weighing the trade — they disengage at first paint. This change strengthens the reason to engage (keeps the warmth alive) WITHOUT removing what they must give or handing the reward over first (which the owner has ruled out).
what_would_have_to_be_true: A meaningful share of the 52% who never type are leaving because the opening feels cold/transactional rather than because they never wanted a next order (ceiling) or distrust the page.
A warmer opening line survives across all SKUs without naming a product or the printed %.
The warmth does not read as gimmicky or delay the reward enough to frustrate the discount-motivated majority.
change.second_order_effects: The email gate is the delivery mechanism for BOTH rewards (unique single-use code via Klaviyo + email-delivered video) and enrollment for Klaviyo review-reminder emails. This change touches none of that machinery — it only rewords the opening — so no reward delivery or review path is put at risk. If it works, MORE emails means more of both review paths downstream; if it does nothing, nothing downstream changes. It does not alter what is promised, when the email is asked, or how rewards are delivered.
change.strongest_case_against: A sceptic would say: the real reason most scanners don't give an email is the ceiling — a one-off gift buyer simply doesn't want a 'next order' discount — and no amount of warm copy fixes a wrong offer, so this is a zero-effect cosmetic tweak; also PR #8 already 'tried the claim page' and it went flat. My answer: (1) PR #8 changed structure/layout, not the opening voice — a different mechanism, and the ONE change that moved this funnel worked by changing motivation, so voice is the more promising lever, not spent ground. (2) I am not claiming this will clear the noise floor (it is labelled unmeasurable); it is a small, reversible, on-brand bet on a cause the data can't yet settle, which is exactly the compounding-experiment this job is built on. (3) If the ceiling dominates, this fix is harmless and the forthcoming never-engaged-vs-declined instrument (readable ~Aug) will tell us, informing the next, larger bet. The cost of being wrong is ~nil; the cost of doing nothing here is another idle cycle on the biggest leak.

tradeoff.gained: More scanners stay engaged at first paint and reach the email ask; if even a few more give an email, both review paths (in-app thank-you + Klaviyo reminders) get more input.
tradeoff.risked: Essentially nothing measurable is put at risk: the change touches no mechanics, no promise, no delivery. Downstream email_redirect review clicks (0 this window, 2 prior) can only rise, not fall, since the email gate is unchanged. Worst realistic case is zero effect.
unverified_assumptions: That the tonal break (not the ceiling or distrust) is the cause driving non-engagement — the data locates WHERE the loss is (first paint) but cannot yet single out WHY; this is an explicit bet, revisited with the ~2026-08-05 never-engaged-vs-declined read.

change.differs_from_past_attempt: Differs from PR #8 (recorded FLAT): PR #8 rebuilt the claim page LAYOUT/HIERARCHY (structure) — this changes only the opening VOICE (one headline + one lead-in), a motivation mechanism, with no layout change. Differs from the owner-REJECTED discount-first idea: it never hands the code over before the email and never defers the gate. Differs from the owner-REJECTED printed-% idea: it never references, quotes, or compares the printed discount number. Differs from last cycle's failed diagnosis: it is not premised on the ~1.2s opening blur, and the session data actively supports (rather than contradicts) first-paint non-engagement.

change.commit_message: feat(claim): open the claim page in a warm voice before the reward ask

pr_body:
## What this changes

The claim page is the screen a customer sees right after scanning the QR code on their gift box. Right now it opens with a cold coupon header — a big gold **"You've Got 30% Off"** and the flat line **"Enter your email to receive"**. The gift box that made them scan, though, is warm and playful ("did this make you smile?"). This change rewords just **two lines** so the page greets people in that same warm voice before it mentions the reward:

- Headline: **"You've Got 30% Off" → "Hope it made you smile"**
- Lead-in above the rewards: **"Enter your email to receive" → "Add your email and we'll send"**

Everything else is untouched — the 30%-off code, the free personalized video, the email box, and the "Send Me My Code" button are all still there, and the discount is shown right below the new headline. See the BEFORE/AFTER photos.

## Why

Our session recordings this fortnight show the loss on this page is at *first sight*: 23 of 44 recorded visits (52%) never typed a single key, and 8 of them clicked nothing at all. People aren't giving up on the form — most never engage it. That points to a motivation problem at first paint, not a form-friction one. History agrees: the one change that ever moved this part of the journey (June 16) worked by changing *meaning/motivation*, while the one layout reshuffle here (PR #8) did nothing. So we're attacking the opening *voice*, which has never been touched, rather than the layout, which has.

## Honest limits — please read as a bet, not a proven fix

At ~12–16 scans a day, a two-line copy change is very unlikely to ever show up as a statistically real move (we can only distinguish swings of ~13–20 points at this traffic). **This is labelled unmeasurable by design.** It's a small, on-brand, instantly-reversible bet — the kind we ship many of, expecting them to compound. No future cycle may claim it "worked" without a significant test result. The recordings tell us *where* people leave (first sight) but not *why* — cold tone vs. "a one-off buyer just doesn't want a next-order discount" vs. distrust all look the same. This bets on the tone being part of it, at essentially zero cost. A more precise read of "never engaged vs. engaged-then-declined" becomes available around **Aug 5** and will aim the next, bigger swing.

## Verdict on the last change (2026-07-06, the create-screen friction fix)

Still **not yet measurable**. The PostHog report that originally graded it is unavailable this cycle (an API permission expired). The nearest durable stand-in, role-picked → video-started, is 62.8% (27 of 43) before vs 56.5% (26 of 46) now — but the two windows aren't comparable (the share of un-linkable sessions moved 21 points) and the move is inside the noise floor anyway: `node tools/significance.mjs 27 43 26 46` → −6.3 pts, p=0.55, NOT SIGNIFICANT. The whole warm stretch (gave email → started video) is flat: 39.4% (28/71) → 41.3% (26/63), `significance.mjs 28 71 26 63` → +1.8 pts, p=0.83, NOT SIGNIFICANT. Verdict carried forward unchanged.

## The leaks, ranked

1. **Claim page: landed → gave email** — the biggest loss by headcount (~115 people/fortnight), right at the top, and the email is the only key to both ways we earn reviews. Only one real prior attempt (a flat layout redesign). **← this change.**
2. **Gave email → started a video** — ~59% of our warmest users still don't start, but it was attacked twice recently and the last change's reading isn't in yet, so piling on now would muddy it.
3. **Preview/share review asks** — basically 0 clicks, but tiny in absolute reviews and reworked once in June with no effect.

## What the reviewer (QA) said and how I responded

Approved, with three minor notes: (1) this is a bet on tone while the data can't yet separate tone from a wrong-offer ceiling — I've framed it explicitly as an unprovable bet and left the verdict open; (2) the premium/warm/no-product-name/no-percentage bar is narrow — the shipped copy carries no product word, no percentage, no emoji, and the owner sees the actual lines in the photos; (3) the "52% never typed" figure is lower than an older ~67% — noted, and the conclusion holds under either number.

## How I verified it

Booted the app locally, loaded the claim page for two different products (a potato and a cat SKU) — both returned OK, both showed the new warm lines, the old cold lines were gone, and the discount + button were still in place with no product name or percentage leaking into the new headline. Rendered mobile BEFORE (live site) and AFTER (this change) screenshots and confirmed only the two lines changed. Cleaned up the two test page-views my screenshots created.

## What to re-measure, and roughly when

Around **Aug 5**, using our own database, re-check two things from the claim page: of everyone who lands, how many even touch the email box, and of those who touch it, how many actually submit — comparing the two weeks after this change to the two weeks before, and running the significance test on each. (The exact commands are recorded in the change log so anyone can reproduce the numbers.) Expect it to stay inside the noise floor — the value here is the compounding of many small honest bets, not this one line item.
telegram_summary:
Last change (07-06 create-screen fix): still NOT yet measurable — gave-email→video flat 39.4%→41.3%, p=0.83; role→video 62.8%→56.5%, p=0.55. Both inside noise.

Top leak: the claim page — most scanners never give an email (~115/fortnight), the only key to both review paths. Recordings: 52% never touch the form — loss is at first sight.

Shipped: reworded the claim page's two opening lines in the gift box's warm voice — headline 'Hope it made you smile' (was 'You've Got 30% Off'), lead-in 'Add your email and we'll send'. Discount, video, email box, button all unchanged. On-brand, reversible, unmeasurable by design — a compounding bet, not called a win without a real test. Photos attached.
